question: Why can altering a ready-made topical cream cause problems?

options.A: It changes the expiration date to the exact same day
options.B: It breaks down the product stability and preservatives
options.C: It automatically turns the lotion into a liquid
options.D: It causes the active ingredient to evaporate instantly

explanation: Mixing products messes up the chemical balance and can make it easier for bacteria to grow. Don't worry, you'll get the hang of product safety in no time!

question: Which specific cells in the testes are responsible for making testosterone?

options.A: Seminiferous tubules
options.B: Bulbourethral glands
options.C: Cells of Leydig
options.D: Epididymis

explanation: Great job! The interstitial cells of Leydig are found inside the testes and do the heavy lifting of making testosterone. Keep it up!

question: Why does the body slow down its metabolism during long periods of starvation?

options.A: To conserve remaining energy stores and prolong survival
options.B: To build up extra muscle tissue in the limbs
options.C: To prepare the digestive tract for a heavy meal
options.D: To increase physical activity levels automatically

explanation: It is a brilliant survival mechanism. When food is scarce, the body dials down its energy use so it doesn't burn through its fat and muscle too fast.

question: Why could it backfire if you only consult wealthy community elites when planning a health project?

options.A: Elites are immune to most common infectious and tropical diseases
options.B: The elites may not represent or understand the actual needs of marginalized groups
options.C: Traditional leaders always forbid modern nursing practices in public spaces
options.D: The local government will fine the clinic for bypassing traditional protocols

explanation: It's easy to miss the struggles of the everyday person if you only talk to the wealthy leaders. Great nurses make sure to listen to voices from every corner of the community!

question: How does social stigma regarding conditions like HIV or mental illness affect patient care?

options.A: It has no measurable impact on how patients seek medical advice
options.B: It encourages communities to support affected patients with open arms
options.C: It drives patients to hide their conditions and avoid seeking early medical help
options.D: It forces government hospitals to provide luxury private wards for them

explanation: You got it! Fear of judgment or gossip makes many people hide their illnesses and stay away from clinics until it's too late.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do before handling chemical disinfectants?

options.A: Performing hand hygiene and putting on protective gear
options.B: Informing the head physician about the cleaning schedule
options.C: Warming the chemical solution in a microwave oven
options.D: Testing the disinfectant flavor on a sterile cotton swab

explanation: Safety first! Protecting your own skin, hands, and airways from harsh chemicals is a must before you start cleaning up the ward.

question: A researcher wants to record the exact physical behaviors of nurses during a sterile dressing change. Which instrument should they use?

options.A: Observational checklist
options.B: Structured interview guide
options.C: Patient satisfaction survey
options.D: Biographical questionnaire

explanation: Observational checklists are ideal for watching and recording specific actions as they happen in real time. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h3)

question: What is a crucial check a nurse must do before giving any mucous membrane medication?

options.A: Instruct the patient to hold their breath for two minutes
options.B: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly over the site
options.C: Crush the medication to speed up local absorption
options.D: Inspect the target membrane for irritation or lesions

explanation: Always take a quick look first! Checking the tissue ensures there are no open sores or heavy irritation that could make absorption painful or unsafe for the patient.

question: What do you call bending the foot so the toes point upward toward the shin?

options.A: Abduction
options.B: Dorsiflexion
options.C: Plantar flexion
options.D: Pronation

explanation: You got it! Dorsiflexion means pulling the ankle up so the top of the foot moves closer to the leg.

question: Why are PMTCT programs heavily prioritized in regions like sub-Saharan Africa?

options.A: Pregnant women in this region refuse standard hospital treatment.
options.B: This region bears the highest burden of pediatric HIV infections.
options.C: Antiretroviral drugs are only manufactured on the African continent.
options.D: Other regions have completely eradicated the human immunodeficiency virus.

explanation: Sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence of women living with HIV, making targeted prevention programs crucial in this part of the world. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h1)

question: How do adult day care homes primarily benefit family caregivers?

options.A: By taking over complete legal and financial responsibility for the client
options.B: By training family members to become licensed practical nurses
options.C: By permanently removing the need for any home-based care
options.D: By offering temporary respite to prevent physical and emotional burnout

explanation: These facilities give family caregivers a necessary break from constant responsibilities, helping them sustain their own health and continue working or managing personal tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which transport mechanism allows maternal antibodies like IgG to cross over and provide passive immunity to the fetus?

options.A: Osmosis
options.B: Pinocytosis
options.C: Simple diffusion
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Large proteins such as IgG are too big to diffuse, so the placental cells engulf them through pinocytosis or receptor-mediated transport. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h3)

question: Why must an unconscious patient be turned to their side when you are cleaning their mouth?

options.A: To prevent liquids from entering the airway and causing choking
options.B: To stop them from rolling off the bed
options.C: To increase blood flow to the facial nerves
options.D: To make it easier to brush the back teeth

explanation: Awesome! Turning them to the side lets water and saliva pool in the cheek and run out safely, rather than choking their airway.

question: Which hormone acts as the main spark to kickstart puberty?

options.A: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.B: Growth hormone-releasing factor
options.C: Adrenocorticotropic hormone
options.D: Thyroid-stimulating hormone

explanation: You've got this! Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) is the master key that opens the hormonal pathway to start puberty. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why does a lack of dystrophin cause muscle damage in Duchenne muscular dystrophy?

options.A: The muscle cell membrane becomes fragile and tears during normal contractions.
options.B: The muscle cells lose their ability to receive nerve impulses from the spinal cord.
options.C: Satellite cells multiply too quickly and crowd out functional muscle tissue.
options.D: Calcium builds up in the cell and immediately dissolves the bones.

explanation: Without dystrophin to absorb the shock, the outer membrane of the muscle cell easily tears every time the muscle contracts. You're building solid clinical knowledge!

question: What primary role does the family unit play in the food supply chain?

options.A: It acts as the final link that consumes and utilizes the food.
options.B: It regulates international trade agreements for agricultural goods.
options.C: It determines large-scale industrial farming methods.
options.D: It sets global market prices for staple crops.

explanation: Families sit at the end of the supply chain, turning raw food into meals and nutrition for household members. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T031#GNS227_U2_T031_h1)

question: Why are informal sector workers in developing regions often at a higher risk for occupational lung disease?

options.A: Government laws completely ban safety masks in local factories
options.B: The tropical climate causes dust particles to become radioactive
options.C: They frequently lack proper personal protective equipment and health monitoring
options.D: Their lungs are naturally weaker than those of corporate office workers

explanation: The absence of safety gear, safety regulations, and routine medical checkups in informal industries greatly increases the risk of chronic lung injury. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which symptom should a recovering patient at home report to their healthcare team right away?

options.A: Slow improvement in overall daily stamina
options.B: New numbness or tingling in the affected limb
options.C: Mild muscle soreness the day after exercise
options.D: Needing extra rest periods during afternoon chores

explanation: You nailed it! Numbness or tingling can mean a nerve is being squished or blood flow is blocked, so it needs a quick check.

question: How should you best care for a pregnant woman who has mild round ligament cramps?

options.A: Prescribing strong pain medications without consulting a doctor
options.B: Telling her to ignore all pain because it is completely imaginary
options.C: Admitting her immediately to the labor ward for IV fluids
options.D: Reassuring her about normal changes and suggesting gentle stretching

explanation: Warm reassurance and simple comfort measures are all that's needed for normal pregnancy aches. Keep up the brilliant work!

question: Why is it important to watch the client's face during passive exercises?

options.A: To check if they are watching the television
options.B: To spot hidden pain or distress when they cannot speak well
options.C: To check how fast their hair is growing
options.D: To see if they need spectacles to read

explanation: Wonderful! Many patients can't tell you when it hurts, so a quick wince or frown on their face tells you everything you need to know.

question: What is the primary definition of homeostasis in the human body?

options.A: Stopping all electrical activity in the brain
options.B: Rapidly fluctuating blood pressure levels
options.C: Constantly increasing metabolic activity
options.D: Maintaining a stable internal environment

explanation: Homeostasis refers to the body's continuous effort to keep its internal conditions stable and balanced despite external changes. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h1)

question: How do diuretic medications help bring down high blood pressure?

options.A: By helping the kidneys remove excess sodium and water
options.B: By blocking calcium entry into arterial wall cells
options.C: By strengthening the pumping force of the left ventricle
options.D: By directly slowing down the electrical conduction of the heart

explanation: Diuretics are 'water pills'! They tell the kidneys to flush out extra salt and water, shrinking the total fluid volume in the pipes so pressure drops.

question: What is another common name for healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Autoimmune disorders
options.B: Idiopathic conditions
options.C: Nosocomial infections
options.D: Congenital infections

explanation: Nosocomial is the traditional medical term for infections that originate in a hospital environment. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h1)

question: Where is the normal point of maximal impulse (PMI) located on a healthy adult chest?

options.A: Second intercostal space at the left sternal border
options.B: Third intercostal space at the right sternal border
options.C: Seventh intercostal space at the anterior axillary line
options.D: Fifth intercostal space at the left midclavicular line

explanation: You'll usually find the normal PMI right at the fifth intercostal space along the left midclavicular line. Excellent clinical landmark! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h7)

question: Why does passing a urinary catheter help when managing postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: It completely stops the flow of blood from the vagina
options.B: A full bladder stops the uterus from contracting effectively
options.C: It allows the nurse to measure exact urine output
options.D: It prevents the patient from getting a urinary tract infection

explanation: An overfull bladder pushes the uterus out of place so it can't contract properly. Empty it out, and the uterus can firm up!

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important in high-risk pregnancy care?

options.A: Patients on bed rest have nothing else to do during the day
options.B: Mental health counseling replaces the need for medical check-ups
options.C: Chronic stress and anxiety can negatively affect both maternal and fetal well-being
options.D: It guarantees the mother will have a natural vaginal delivery

explanation: Mind and body are connected! High stress releases hormones that can impact the pregnancy, so a comforting word from you as a nurse goes a long way.

question: A patient has an ideal body weight of 70 kg. Which tidal volume setting falls within the safe lung-protective range?

options.A: 750 mL
options.B: 450 mL
options.C: 900 mL
options.D: 250 mL

explanation: Protective ventilation uses 6 to 8 mL per kg. For a 70 kg patient, that's roughly 420 to 560 mL, making 450 mL a safe and correct choice!

question: What is the main chemical messenger used by the endocrine system?

options.A: Enzymes
options.B: Electrolytes
options.C: Neurotransmitters
options.D: Hormones

explanation: Spot on! Endocrine glands release hormones straight into the bloodstream to help regulate how different parts of the body work.

question: Special parietal cells in the stomach secrete a substance you need to absorb vitamin B12. What is it called?

options.A: Gastric mucus
options.B: Intrinsic factor
options.C: Pepsinogen
options.D: Hydrochloric acid

explanation: You're doing great! Intrinsic factor acts like a VIP ticket for vitamin B12, helping the lower small intestine absorb it properly.

question: What does a cracking or grating sound in a joint (called crepitus) usually mean?

options.A: Rapid healing of a fracture through callus tissue
options.B: Rough bone ends grinding against each other
options.C: Excessive accumulation of healthy synovial fluid
options.D: Normal sliding of smooth articular cartilage

explanation: Crepitus is that crunching feeling you get when the smooth cartilage is gone and bare bones scrape together during movement.

question: What is the most important daily habit for preventing foot complications in a patient with nerve loss?

options.A: Inspecting the feet daily for cuts, blisters, and pressure injuries
options.B: Encouraging barefoot walking indoors to stimulate deep tendon reflexes
options.C: Massaging the toes vigorously with alcohol twice a day
options.D: Applying high-strength heating pads to the calves every evening

explanation: When you can't feel your feet, small cuts can turn into big, infected sores without you noticing. Daily checks catch little problems before they become emergencies!

question: A woman with severe bleeding after childbirth dies because the clinic has no blood and no ambulance to transfer her. Which delay caused this?

options.A: Zero delay
options.B: Third delay
options.C: Second delay
options.D: First delay

explanation: The third delay happens right inside the health facility when care is delayed or inadequate because of shortages in supplies, equipment, or trained staff. You're doing great learning these concepts!

question: Which of these conditions is most likely to need a surgical valve repair or replacement?

options.A: Simple ventricular ectopic beats
options.B: Severe aortic stenosis
options.C: Controlled essential hypertension
options.D: Mild sinus tachycardia

explanation: When a valve is severely narrowed (stenosis), blood can't get through properly. Surgery is often needed to fix or replace that physical blockage.

question: What does Type IV FGM involve?

options.A: Surgical reconstruction of damaged labial tissue
options.B: Pricking, piercing, scraping, or cauterizing the genital area
options.C: Complete removal of the uterus and ovaries
options.D: Routine episiotomy performed during childbirth

explanation: Type IV is the catch-all category for any other harmful, non-medical tinkering with female genitalia. Every question you answer makes you a sharper nurse!

question: You just finished giving an injection. Where should you drop the used syringe and needle?

options.A: A puncture-proof yellow safety box
options.B: An open plastic basin on the trolley
options.C: A black household polythene bag
options.D: A brown pharmaceutical waste bin

explanation: Brilliant! Sharps always go straight into a rigid, puncture-proof safety box to prevent accidental needle pricks. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h7)

question: When are most anthelminthic drugs strictly avoided due to risks to the baby?

options.A: During the final weeks of breastfeeding
options.B: During the first trimester of pregnancy
options.C: In patients over sixty-five years of age
options.D: Throughout the entire adolescent period

explanation: Spot on! Since the baby's vital organs are forming during the first trimester, we generally avoid these drugs to keep the foetus safe.

question: A 30-year smoker comes in with severe breathlessness and a chronic cough. Which condition affecting the tiny air sacs is most likely the cause?

options.A: Acute bronchitis
options.B: Bacterial pneumonia
options.C: Emphysema
options.D: Pulmonary embolism

explanation: Long-term smoking destroys the delicate walls of the alveoli (air sacs), leading to emphysema and trapped air. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: When is a nurse legally and ethically allowed to break an adolescent's confidentiality?

options.A: Whenever the teenager admits to eating junk food at school
options.B: When there is a clear danger of severe abuse or self-harm
options.C: Whenever a parent asks what happened during the consultation
options.D: When the adolescent misses a scheduled follow-up appointment

explanation: Confidentiality must be broken only when the physical safety and immediate welfare of the young person are seriously threatened. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h4)

question: Why does empowering women often lead to smaller, more planned families?

options.A: Employers legally restrict female workers from starting families
options.B: Women lose their biological capacity to conceive after higher education
options.C: Women gain greater decision-making power over their reproductive health
options.D: Government laws force educated women to have fewer children

explanation: Spot on! When women are empowered, they have a stronger voice in deciding family size and birth spacing.

question: Which artery provides the main blood supply to the abdominal section of the oesophagus?

options.A: Right subclavian artery
options.B: Left gastric artery
options.C: Descending thoracic aorta
options.D: Inferior thyroid artery

explanation: You're learning fast! As the oesophagus drops down into the belly area, it picks up its blood supply mostly from branches of the left gastric artery.

question: Which everyday or routine activity carries a real risk of transmitting HIV?

options.A: Sharing eating utensils and drinking cups at a family dinner
options.B: Sharing intravenous drug injection needles with an infected person
options.C: Receiving a hug or handshake from an infected coworker
options.D: Swimming in the same public pool as a person with HIV

explanation: HIV spreads through direct blood-to-blood contact, such as sharing needles. Casual contact like hugging or sharing spoons is completely safe!

question: Why do patients with advanced HIV catch unusual bugs like Pneumocystis pneumonia?

options.A: Their weakened immune systems cannot fight off normal environmental organisms.
options.B: The virus directly mutates lung tissue into cancerous cells.
options.C: Antiretroviral drugs cause severe respiratory tract paralysis.
options.D: Red blood cells lose their ability to carry oxygen to the lungs.

explanation: These are called opportunistic infections—they take advantage of a weak immune system to cause sickness.

question: How should you best communicate with an older adult who has mild hearing loss?

options.A: Speaking very quickly to get through the assessment faster
options.B: Shouting loudly directly into the patient's ear canal
options.C: Writing everything down on a board and avoiding speech
options.D: Facing the patient directly and speaking in a normal tone

explanation: Spot on! Facing them lets them read your lips and facial expressions, whereas shouting can distort the sound and cause embarrassment.

question: What is the main goal of home health nursing care?

options.A: Transitioning every patient back to an acute care ward
options.B: Replacing all care previously given by family members
options.C: Promoting recovery and managing chronic conditions
options.D: Providing permanent 24-hour nursing supervision

explanation: Home health nursing focuses on helping patients recover from illness or manage ongoing conditions right where they live, avoiding unnecessary hospital stays. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which annoying side effect is very common with ACE inhibitors and often makes patients switch to ARBs?

options.A: Sudden severe hair loss
options.B: Yellowing of the eyes
options.C: Tremors in both hands
options.D: A persistent dry cough

explanation: Spot on! ACE inhibitors can cause a buildup of a substance called bradykinin in the lungs. It's harmless, but that tickly, dry cough can drive patients crazy!

question: A patient is using their neck and shoulder muscles heavily to take every breath. What does this sign indicate?

options.A: The patient has a normal, healthy breathing pattern
options.B: The patient's lungs are expanding with minimal effort
options.C: The patient is in a deeply relaxed sleeping state
options.D: The patient is experiencing increased respiratory effort and distress

explanation: Using accessory muscles means the main breathing muscles need extra help because breathing has become difficult. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is one of the main duties of a community health nurse regarding occupational safety?

options.A: Educating workers on hazard recognition and protective gear
options.B: Designing industrial machinery for manufacturing companies
options.C: Enforcing labor laws through police intervention
options.D: Managing the financial accounts of private factories

explanation: Community nurses shine at health education—teaching everyday workers how to spot dangers and use protective gear correctly.

question: Why do whole fruits cause a slower, safer rise in blood sugar than fruit juices?

options.A: Whole fruits contain zero natural sugars unlike juice
options.B: The intact fiber slows down digestion and sugar absorption
options.C: Teexh enzymes block sugar from entering the bloodstream
options.D: Stomach acid instantly destroys all fruit sugars

explanation: Correct! The natural fiber in whole fruits acts like a speed bump, helping your body absorb the sugar nice and slowly.

question: Why do mucous membranes absorb medicines so quickly?

options.A: An absence of epithelial tissue
options.B: High levels of gastric acid
options.C: A thick outer layer of dry skin
options.D: A rich network of blood vessels

explanation: Think of mucous membranes like a busy market with delivery vans parked right at the gate! They have lots of tiny blood vessels close to the surface, so drugs get picked up and carried into the bloodstream in no time.

question: What does the letter 'D' stand for in the HEADSS adolescent assessment tool?

options.A: Drugs, alcohol, and tobacco use
options.B: Depression and developmental delays
options.C: Diet, disease, and daily exercise
options.D: Discipline at school and home

explanation: In the HEADSS screening tool, 'D' stands for drugs, alcohol, and tobacco use habits. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why do we involve family members so closely in Community-Based Rehabilitation?

options.A: Families provide continuous daily support and reinforce therapy goals
options.B: Families are legally required to pay for all hospital equipment
options.C: Nurses prefer to avoid visiting patients at home
options.D: Community members lack basic literacy skills

explanation: Since care continues outside the hospital, family members are your greatest allies in making sure the patient keeps up with their daily exercises and routines.

question: Which of these duties should a registered nurse NEVER delegate to an untrained ward assistant?

options.A: Conducting a comprehensive initial clinical assessment of a new patient
options.B: Measuring and recording the body temperature of a stable patient
options.C: Changing clean bed linens for a patient on bed rest
options.D: Serving pre-packaged food trays to admitted patients

explanation: Initial patient assessments require professional nursing judgment and clinical thinking, which only trained nurses can do.

question: What does 'clinical significance' mean in simple terms when looking at drug research?

options.A: Whether the research paper was published in an international journal
options.B: Whether the study results make a meaningful, noticeable difference to the patient's health
options.C: Whether the pharmaceutical company made a profit from the drug trial
options.D: Whether the mathematical formula used in the data analysis was complex enough

explanation: Well done! Numbers might show a tiny statistical change, but clinical significance means the patient actually feels or gets better in real life.

question: Which of the following is a common operational barrier to implementing clinical standards in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Shortages of essential equipment and supplies
options.B: A complete absence of hospital patients
options.C: Too much free time during morning shifts
options.D: An excess of available nursing personnel on every shift

explanation: Without basic tools like gloves, clean water, or drugs, nurses struggle to follow clinical standards properly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h6)

question: What tool can nurses use to help patients estimate portion sizes more accurately?

options.A: A standard household measuring cup for liquid medications only
options.B: A complex laboratory blood test for vitamin levels
options.C: Visual aids like food models or picture charts
options.D: Strict financial receipts from local grocery stores

explanation: Patients often struggle to describe portion sizes in grams or cups, so visual aids make it easier for them to show how much they ate. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h8)

question: How does gender inequality directly contribute to early marriage?

options.A: By forcing boys to leave school early to work
options.B: By limiting educational opportunities for young girls
options.C: By granting young females absolute control over family assets
options.D: By making traditional marriage ceremonies illegal

explanation: When girls are denied education and future opportunities, society often pushes them straight into early marriage instead.

question: When is a gastrostomy tube usually chosen over a nasogastric tube?

options.A: When the patient only needs overnight hydration for a few days
options.B: When the patient is expected to resume normal eating within a week
options.C: When the stomach is surgically removed due to severe ulcer disease
options.D: When tube feeding is needed for longer than four to six weeks

explanation: Long-term enteral nutrition relies on gastrostomy tubes because they are more stable and comfortable than nasal tubes for extended use. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h1)

question: You are caring for a stroke patient. Which of these signs needs your immediate action to stop a life-threatening problem?

options.A: Coughing and wet-sounding voice while drinking water
options.B: A minor loss of memory regarding recent visitors
options.C: Slight weakness in the right upper and lower extremities
options.D: Mild frustration when attempting to button a shirt

explanation: Coughing or a gurgly voice right after drinking is a huge red flag for swallowing trouble (dysphagia). It means water might be going down the wrong pipe into the lungs, risking aspiration pneumonia!

question: Which of the following describes a primary data collection method?

options.A: Reading a published textbook summary of historical mortality rates
options.B: Interviewing patients directly after surgery for a new study
options.C: Downloading a public census file from a government website
options.D: Extracting anonymized blood pressure logs from old hospital archives

explanation: Primary data is gathered firsthand by the researcher specifically to answer their own current research question. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the main goal of giving medications for chronic, degenerative diseases like Parkinson's or Alzheimer's?

options.A: To manage ongoing physical and mental decline
options.B: To completely cure the underlying genetic defect
options.C: To permanently stop the normal aging process
options.D: To wipe out sudden bacterial infections in the tissues

explanation: You've got this! Because degenerative diseases cause gradual wear and tear on the body, medications are used to slow things down and help patients manage daily life, rather than providing a quick cure.

question: What is the purpose of adding hyaluronic acid to an arthritic joint?

options.A: To permanently numb the nerves of the entire leg
options.B: To kill bacterial infections inside the joint capsule
options.C: To permanently fuse the joint bones together
options.D: To act as a viscosupplement and improve joint lubrication

explanation: Hyaluronic acid mimics natural joint fluid to provide cushioning and smooth movement. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is the main goal of a safe injection according to the WHO?

options.A: To completely eliminate the use of oral medications in the hospital
options.B: To prevent harm to the patient and worker without creating dangerous waste
options.C: To ensure medications are absorbed twice as fast into the bloodstream
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing disposable syringes

explanation: A safe injection protects everyone: the patient getting the drug, you as the nurse giving it, and the community from bad waste disposal. You've got this!

question: Why is emotional and psychological support an important part of long-term care for pacemaker patients?

options.A: Emotional support prevents the pacemaker leads from coming loose in the heart
options.B: Mental stress directly drains the electrical battery inside the chest wall
options.C: Psychological counseling is legally required before every battery replacement
options.D: Patients often experience anxiety and fear regarding device failure or lifestyle limits

explanation: Living with a device in your chest can be scary. Being a supportive nurse means caring for their emotional worries just as much as their physical heart!

question: What is the main reason lab technicians spin urine in a machine (centrifuge) before looking at it under a microscope?

options.A: To kill any live bacteria that might distort the viewing field
options.B: To concentrate solid particles at the bottom into a sediment pellet
options.C: To break down large protein strands that block the microscope lens
options.D: To raise the temperature of the sample for better chemical reactivity

explanation: Centrifuging acts like a quick spin cycle that gathers all the heavy cells, crystals, and casts neatly at the bottom of the tube so they are super easy to spot and study.

question: During a measles outbreak, why do public health teams do 'contact tracing'?

options.A: To collect financial penalties for spreading the infection
options.B: To monitor exposed individuals during the incubation period and offer vaccination
options.C: To test the water supply for bacterial contamination
options.D: To punish individuals who failed to attend the primary health clinic

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Tracing contacts lets nurses catch infections early and vaccinate people before symptoms appear.

question: Why shouldn't patients cover skin creams with airtight plastic wraps unless a doctor tells them to?

options.A: It prevents the cream from ever touching the skin surface
options.B: It can trap excessive moisture and increase drug absorption dangerously
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling any local pain relief
options.D: It causes the skin to become permanently discolored

explanation: Airtight wraps act like an oven, trapping heat and moisture, which forces too much medicine into the body all at once. Spot on!

question: When monitoring vital signs in a patient with suspected internal bleeding, what is most important to look for?

options.A: A single normal blood pressure reading
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: An increase in respiratory depth only
options.D: Trends indicating a worsening condition over time

explanation: Observing how vital signs change sequentially gives a much clearer picture of ongoing blood loss than looking at one isolated set of numbers. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h4)

question: An elderly male patient after surgery is restless and feels a strong urge to pee, but nothing comes out. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Stress incontinence
options.B: Renal tubular acidosis
options.C: Urinary retention
options.D: Transitional hyperplasia

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! When a patient feels the urge but can't pass urine and is restless, think urinary retention first. You'll be checking for a distended bladder often in surgical wards!

question: A patient with severe malaria is worried about losing income and how their family will eat while they are in the hospital. Which dimension of care is primarily affected here?

options.A: Mental dimension
options.B: Physical dimension
options.C: Social dimension
options.D: Spiritual dimension

explanation: Spot on! Family roles, financial worries, and community support fall squarely under the social dimension of human life.

question: Which sign points strongly to a wound infection after a skin biopsy?

question: What does a pale inner eyelid or pale nail bed usually point to?

options.A: High blood pressure
options.B: Dehydration
options.C: Anaemia
options.D: An infection

explanation: Paleness in the mucous membranes and nails is a classic sign that the red blood cell count or haemoglobin is low, which we call anaemia.

question: Which detail is most important to include in your notes when charting routine hair care?

options.A: The exact minute the hair drying process started
options.B: Condition of the scalp and any abnormal findings
options.C: The total cost of the hair care products used
options.D: The exact brand of shampoo preferred by the nurse

explanation: Always focus your documentation on clear clinical facts, such as how the scalp looks and any unusual signs you spot. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: What important detail must be included when documenting an intradermal injection?

options.A: Brand name of the alcohol swab
options.B: Name of the nurse's supervisor
options.C: Patient's favorite arm preference
options.D: Exact anatomical site used

explanation: Recording the exact location is necessary so the healthcare team can find the correct spot when returning to read the test results. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which of these is a clear example of objective data?

options.A: A feeling of dizziness upon standing up quickly
options.B: A body temperature reading of 38.5 degrees Celsius
options.C: A statement of anxiety about upcoming surgery
options.D: A patient reporting a dull ache in the lower back

explanation: Objective data is what you can actually see, touch, or measure yourself (like a thermometer reading), unlike feelings that only the patient can tell you about.

question: What is the primary hormone secreted by the hypothalamus that starts the reproductive hormone chain?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.D: Testosterone

explanation: The hypothalamus releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland, which drives the entire reproductive hormone pathway. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why do we divide an operating suite into unrestricted, semi-restricted, and restricted zones?

options.A: To progressively lower the risk of microbial contamination closer to the patient
options.B: To ensure that doctors and nurses have separate break rooms
options.C: To make it easier to clean the floors with automated machines
options.D: To prevent patients from wandering into the administrative offices

explanation: You got it! These zoning layers act like security checkpoints, filtering out dust and germs step-by-step before anyone steps near the patient.

question: What part of the male genitalia is removed during circumcision?

options.A: The urethral meatus
options.B: The foreskin
options.C: The penile shaft skin
options.D: The scrotal sac

question: What is a standard check done during a routine antenatal clinic (ANC) visit?

options.A: Screening for lifelong hereditary blood disorders
options.B: Performing routine pelvic ultrasounds every week
options.C: Checking maternal blood pressure and urine protein
options.D: Measuring daily caloric intake and physical activity

explanation: Spotting changes in blood pressure and checking urine for protein helps us catch early signs of pre-eclampsia. Great nursing practice! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h3)

question: What is the main public health strategy used worldwide to wipe out onchocerciasis?

options.A: Mass vaccination campaigns with live attenuated virus
options.B: Daily antibiotic prophylaxis for all infants
options.C: Community-directed treatment with ivermectin
options.D: Complete relocation of riverbank settlements

question: A patient has sharp, severe tummy pain that hurts much worse when they move or take a deep breath. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Irritation of the parietal peritoneum
options.B: Slow movement in the large bowel
options.C: Normal gas movement through the colon
options.D: Stretching of a hollow organ muscle

explanation: The parietal peritoneum has lots of somatic nerve fibers that react sharply to movement and inflammation, causing that localized, sharp pain.

question: If a seriously ill child has a completely normal blood pressure reading, does that mean they are out of danger?

options.A: Fluid resuscitation is definitely not needed
options.B: The child is completely free from danger
options.C: Cardiac output is at its absolute maximum
options.D: The child may still be in compensated shock

explanation: Kids are amazing at squeezing their blood vessels tight to keep their blood pressure looking normal, even when they are crashing. A normal BP doesn't mean they aren't in shock!

question: Why should a nurse avoid raising the legs of a patient experiencing cardiogenic shock?

options.A: It immediately causes a dangerous drop in blood pressure
options.B: It restricts the movement of the diaphragm and causes choking
options.C: It can overload a failing heart with too much venous return
options.D: It prevents the administration of intravenous medications

explanation: Raising the legs dumps blood back toward the core, which strains a damaged heart muscle that cannot pump effectively. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h5)

question: What makes a nursing care plan truly 'individualized' in holistic practice?

options.A: Writing the care plan in medical jargon the patient cannot understand
options.B: Leaving all care planning decisions entirely up to the attending physician
options.C: Using the exact same printed template for every patient with malaria
options.D: Tailoring goals and interventions to the patient's unique lifestyle and values

explanation: That's right! An individualized care plan respects the specific background, preferences, and personal goals of each unique patient.

question: What is the main function of the epididymis?

options.A: Neutralize acidic urine in the urethra
options.B: Allow sperm to mature and gain motility
options.C: Secrete the majority of seminal fluid
options.D: Produce primary male sex hormones

explanation: Sperm entering the epididymis are not yet able to swim; they store there while maturing and acquiring motility. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why does a nurse test tear pH with paper before treating a chemical splash?

options.A: To determine if the patient needs local numbing eye drops first
options.B: To prove that the patient is experiencing a severe allergic reaction
options.C: To measure how severe the chemical exposure is and guide treatment
options.D: To check if the patient has a hidden bacterial eye infection

explanation: Checking the pH tells you if it was an acid or an alkali burn, and you keep washing until the pH goes back to normal. Smart nursing!

question: Why do we actually study nursing theories in school? What is their main job?

options.A: To dictate how much medication a patient should receive
options.B: To eliminate the need for doctor and nurse collaboration
options.C: To guide clinical practice and provide a scientific base
options.D: To replace hospital policies and procedure manuals

explanation: Think of nursing theories as the bedrock of our profession! They give us a clear, scientific reason for the way we care for patients every single day.

question: When doing a thoracentesis, where should the needle enter the chest to keep blood vessels and nerves safe?

options.C: Over the upper border of the lower rib
options.D: Through the soft center of the sternum bone

question: Which sign strongly suggests a patient's sting site is developing a bacterial infection days later?

options.A: Spreading erythema, warmth, and purulent discharge at the site days later

options.C: Clear fluid blisters that form and heal within twenty-four hours
options.D: A small drop in blood pressure within the first five minutes

explanation: Watch out for spreading redness (erythema), feeling hot to the touch, and pus (purulent discharge)—these are classic signs that bacteria have set in.

question: What is the primary vector responsible for transmitting Lassa fever in endemic regions?

options.A: Multimammate rats
options.B: Domesticated pigs
options.C: Tsetse flies
options.D: Anopheles mosquitoes

question: What is the main job of the neurotransmitter GABA when you fall asleep?

options.A: Increasing body temperature and heart rate
options.B: Inhibiting wakefulness centers to allow rest
options.C: Triggering the release of cortisol
options.D: Stimulating the reticular activating system

explanation: GABA is your brain's main calming chemical. It dials down the wake-up centers so you can finally relax and sleep.

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty in teenage boys?

options.A: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.B: A sudden surge in testosterone and related hormones
options.C: The full closure of the growth plates in long bones
options.D: An increase in the production of red blood cells

question: What type of tissue gradually replaces elastic muscle fibers in the uterus after many pregnancies?

options.A: Smooth muscle tissue

options.C: Fibrous connective tissue
options.D: Adipose fatty tissue

question: What happens during the progressive stage of shock?

options.A: Organs begin to regenerate damaged cells rapidly
options.B: Compensatory mechanisms fail and blood pressure drops
options.C: The body completely recovers its normal metabolic rate
options.D: Blood pressure rises above normal due to fluid retention

question: What is a major, life-altering complication frequently linked to advanced endometriosis?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Infertility
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Systemic hypertension

explanation: Due to scarring and ongoing inflammation, getting pregnant can become a real hurdle for many women battling advanced endometriosis.

question: What is the main focus of palliative care for a patient with a terminal neurodegenerative disease?

options.A: Finding a surgical cure for the condition
options.B: Providing comfort and managing symptoms
options.C: Reversing the physical damage to the brain
options.D: Testing new experimental medications

explanation: Palliative care is all about wrapping the patient and family in comfort, easing pain, and giving them the best possible quality of life. Wonderful job completing this set today!

question: What key visual finding does a clinician look for on the cervix during a speculum exam for acute cervicitis?

question: How does the lower esophageal sphincter help protect you from GERD (heartburn)?

options.A: It acts like a muscular valve that stops stomach acid from flowing upward
options.B: It neutralizes food before it drops into the stomach
options.C: It secretes thick mucus to coat the top of the stomach
options.D: It controls how fast food leaves the stomach for the small intestine

explanation: The lower esophageal sphincter is your body's one-way valve. It stays tightly closed and only opens to let food travel down into the stomach.

question: Using the Rule of Nines, what percentage of the total body surface area does an adult's entire front chest and abdomen (anterior trunk) cover?

options.A: 36 percent
options.B: 18 percent
options.C: 9 percent
options.D: 27 percent

explanation: The Rule of Nines is a classic! The front trunk is 18 percent, and the back trunk is also 18 percent. Easy points for your exams!

question: How does teaching communities about health help cut down on self-medication?

options.A: It lowers the market prices of imported pharmaceutical tablets
options.B: It gives every citizen a license to prescribe drugs to their neighbors
options.C: It helps people recognize when symptoms require a professional medical evaluation

question: How should a patient lie during a standard percutaneous liver biopsy?

question: Why must a nurse catch postpartum infections early?

options.A: Postpartum infections can quickly escalate into systemic illness and shock

options.C: Delayed involution of the uterus is the only complication that ever occurs

explanation: Spotting an infection early makes a huge difference! A localized postpartum infection can quickly turn into severe sepsis if we don't catch and treat it promptly.

question: Why do public health nurses and planners care about measuring disease incidence?

options.A: It provides the exact medical cure for infected patients
options.B: It shows if a disease outbreak is growing or shrinking
options.C: It replaces the need for routine vaccination programs
options.D: It calculates the total hospital building costs needed

question: A village floods every rainy season. What is the best proactive nursing action to prepare?

options.A: Focusing solely on treating broken bones after the flood recedes

options.C: Waiting until the floodwaters rise before requesting relief materials
options.D: Educating residents on evacuation routes and establishing early warning systems

question: In male patients, why must you push the catheter a bit further in even after urine first starts to flow?

question: Why must nurses work alongside community leaders when trying to stop breast ironing?

options.C: Law enforcement officers refuse to speak directly with victims

question: Why is community profiling necessary before launching a health project?

options.D: It reveals the unique demographics and culture of the area

question: A patient tells you they feel extremely panicked and short of breath at the thought of entering a narrow, enclosed scanner. What is your best first action?

options.A: Tell the patient to close their eyes and ignore the fear

question: Which of these is a direct clinical duty for a nurse caring for an FGM survivor?

options.A: Performing corrective cosmetic surgeries in outpatient wards

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing one's diet?

question: What is the main goal of an ACTH stimulation test when checking for adrenal insufficiency?

question: A patient with a painful ankle gout flare says even the bedsheet touching the skin is agonizing. What should the nurse do?

question: How is Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) viewed under international human rights law?

options.A: An acceptable alternative traditional medicine practice

question: Why is it important for a nurse to assess a patient's spiritual needs even if they do not share the same religious beliefs?

options.B: To satisfy mandatory legal requirements for hospital discharge

question: What does the acronym ISBAR stand for in emergency handover communication?

question: During a sudden emergency on the ward, the charge nurse gives quick, direct orders without debating. What leadership style is this?

question: What does an Apgar score of 5 at one minute mean for a newborn?

question: Why must a healthcare plan include flexibility?

question: How should a nurse document what a patient says about experiencing abuse?

question: Which hormone tells the Leydig cells in the testes to start producing testosterone?

question: Which family structure typically has a wide pool of available caregivers living close by?

question: What is the main goal of practicing medical asepsis (clean technique) on the ward?

question: What is formed at the very end of the clotting process to firmly seal a damaged blood vessel?

question: What happens during tubular reabsorption in the nephron?

question: Why is it important to assess the patient's perception before delivering bad news?

question: What does tumor 'staging' mainly tell the healthcare team?

question: How does widespread tobacco use create a double challenge for Nigeria's health system?

question: Which harmless temporary side effect do many clients experience during their first few months on the pill?

question: When is the best time to check back on a patient after giving them oral pain medication?

question: Why does HIV specifically attack CD4+ T-cells and macrophages?

question: What does drug tolerance mean?

question: What is the main job of hormones in our bodies?

question: Why do adolescent girls need more iron in their diet?

question: What is the medical term for heavy, prolonged menstrual bleeding, which is very common in women with fibroids?

question: When would you as a nurse request a backrest device for your patient?

question: How does hiring discrimination typically affect a person with a physical disability?

question: What do anticoagulant medications actually do in the body?
