options.D: Prevent the formation of new blood clots

explanation: Think of anticoagulants as your body's stop sign for new clots. They don't break down clots that are already there, but they stop new ones from forming or getting bigger!

question: How can you, as a bedside nurse, help improve injection safety standards in your clinic?

options.A: By buying new safety syringes with your own personal money
options.B: By reporting unsafe practices and joining safety audits
options.C: By handling all medical waste disposal completely alone
options.D: By refusing to give any injections during night shifts

explanation: Well done! Speaking up about risks and taking part in safety checks helps fix system flaws and protects everyone. You're thinking like a professional nurse! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h9)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse just brush off sudden confusion in an older patient as 'normal aging'?

options.A: It violates hospital discharge policies for elderly patients
options.B: It can cause the nurse to miss a treatable underlying medical problem
options.C: It always leads to immediate legal action from family members
options.D: It speeds up the natural physical decline of the brain

explanation: Never assume confusion is just old age! Sudden changes in mental status can be signs of something serious and treatable, like an infection, stroke, or delirium. Always investigate further.

question: Why might a severely anemic patient NOT show a blue skin color (cyanosis) even when their oxygen is dangerously low?

options.A: Their skin is naturally thicker and hides color changes better
options.B: Anemia causes the blood vessels to dilate and turn the skin red instead
options.C: They do not have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to display the blue color
options.D: Their lungs absorb extra oxygen from the surrounding air

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Cyanosis needs enough hemoglobin (the stuff in red blood cells that carries oxygen) to show that blue tint. If a patient is severely anemic, they simply don't have enough to show the color!

question: Which symptom is a major warning sign for bladder cancer?

options.A: Painless gross hematuria
options.B: Painful swelling of the knee joints
options.C: Complete inability to sweat
options.D: Severe sudden right-side flank pain

explanation: Gross hematuria means blood in the urine that you can actually see with the naked eye. When it comes on without any pain, it's a classic red flag for the bladder.

question: What is a major risk if a patient with severe vulvitis keeps scratching the itchy area?

options.A: Sudden systemic high blood pressure
options.B: Permanent loss of bladder control
options.C: Complete closure of the vaginal canal
options.D: Secondary bacterial infection through broken skin

explanation: Scratching breaks the delicate skin barrier, turning a simple itch into an open door for bacteria to sneak in and cause a secondary infection. Patient education on this is so crucial!

question: What is the main reason doctors order a skin snip test?

options.A: Detecting dermal microfilariae of Onchocerca volvulus
options.B: Culturing bacterial pathogens in cellulitis
options.C: Measuring deep dermal thickness for burn assessment
options.D: Identifying fungal elements in superficial tinea

explanation: You got this! A skin snip is specifically used to catch tiny parasite larvae (microfilariae) hiding in the skin layers.

question: Why do blood sugar levels shoot up quickly during a sympathetic response?

options.A: To provide immediate cellular energy for muscles to react
options.B: To feed the digestive system for faster food processing
options.C: To satisfy sudden hunger cravings caused by stress
options.D: To cool down the body temperature during physical exertion

explanation: Your body breaks down stored sugar (glycogen) fast so your muscles have instant fuel to run or fight. Smart design by nature!

question: How does the body naturally balance out the forward pull of a growing belly?

options.A: By leaning the upper torso and shoulders backward
options.B: By increasing the calcium density in the lower leg bones
options.C: By shortening the overall length of the spinal column
options.D: By bending the knees forward at all times

explanation: Leaning backward helps the mother keep her balance over her feet, though it places extra stress on the back muscles. Think of it as a natural balancing act!

question: Which of the following describes economic violence in a domestic relationship?

options.A: Splitting utility bills evenly between two working adults
options.B: Forgetting to consult a partner before making a household purchase
options.C: Donating family savings to a charity without asking
options.D: Controlling access to money and preventing a partner from working

explanation: Economic abuse involves financial control, making the survivor entirely dependent on the abuser for survival. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h2)

question: What does the letter 'A' stand for in the emergency assessment framework ABCDE?

options.A: Activity
options.B: Airway
options.C: Anxiety
options.D: Antibiotic

explanation: Checking the airway is always the first step in any emergency to make sure air can flow freely into the lungs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h6)

question: How can pouring leftover drugs down open drains harm our environment?

options.A: It triggers severe volcanic activity near water bodies
options.B: It contributes to antimicrobial resistance and harms aquatic life
options.C: It instantly freezes local rivers and kills vegetation
options.D: It causes immediate radioactive contamination in the soil

explanation: Drugs in our waterways expose local water animals and bacteria to medications, helping drug-resistant superbugs grow faster.

question: A digital monitor shows a very high blood pressure for a calm patient who feels totally fine. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Write down the machine's number and walk away to another room
options.B: Check the reading manually using a stethoscope and manual cuff
options.C: Rush to give the patient strong blood pressure-lowering drugs
options.D: Throw the electronic device away and never use it again

explanation: Machines can glitch! If a result doesn't match how the patient looks or feels, always double-check it manually before panicking or treating.

question: Which of these medications is a well-known first-generation (typical) antipsychotic?

options.A: Haloperidol
options.B: Olanzapine
options.C: Quetiapine
options.D: Risperidone

explanation: Haloperidol is a classic typical antipsychotic you'll see used very often in hospital wards for acute agitation and severe psychosis.

question: What does the first menstrual period (menarche) mainly tell us about a young girl?

options.A: Full adult nutritional stores
options.B: Maximum skeletal height achievement
options.C: The beginning of reproductive capability
options.D: Complete closure of the pelvic growth plates

explanation: Well done! Menarche shows her body can now release eggs, but remember: it doesn't mean her pelvic bones are fully grown for safe childbirth yet.

question: Why are nurses in such a great position to catch adverse drug reactions early?

options.A: They are legally responsible for manufacturing all hospital drugs
options.B: They maintain close, continuous contact with hospitalized patients
options.C: They perform all laboratory blood chemistry tests
options.D: They set the retail prices for pharmaceuticals in Nigeria

explanation: Because you spend the most time right at the bedside, you are usually the first to notice early physical or mood changes after a patient takes a drug.

question: What type of water is best for soaking Plaster of Paris bandages?

options.A: Ice cold water
options.B: Boiling hot water
options.C: Carbonated water
options.D: Lukewarm water

explanation: Lukewarm water gives you a predictable setting time. Hot water makes it set way too fast, and cold water slows it right down.

question: Poor waste disposal and unsafe drinking water lead directly to which group of diseases?

options.A: Genetic blood disorders like sickle cell anemia
options.B: Fecal-oral diseases like cholera and typhoid
options.C: Airborne infections like tuberculosis
options.D: Sexually transmitted infections

explanation: You got it! When sanitation fails, germs from human waste easily find their way into drinking water, spreading nasty tummy bugs.

question: A patient with a leg cast has severe pain, and their toes look pale and feel cool. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a complete neurovascular assessment and notify the physician immediately.
options.B: Remove the cast immediately using an electric cutting saw at the bedside.
options.C: Reassure the patient that this is a completely normal reaction to a cast.
options.D: Administer a stronger sleeping tablet and wait until the morning shift.

explanation: Pale, cool toes and severe pain are red flags! They mean blood flow or nerves might be squeezed too tight by the cast. Quick assessment and calling the doctor can save the limb.

question: How would you explain a negative feedback loop of hormones to a curious patient?

options.A: It allows the brain to control your heart rate and breathing rate simultaneously.
options.B: It prevents the testes from ever changing in size throughout your lifetime.
options.C: It stops the body from producing too much testosterone when levels are already high.
options.D: It ensures that the pituitary gland stops working completely during physical rest.

explanation: Think of it like an air conditioner thermostat! When hormone levels get high enough, a signal goes back to the brain to slow things down so the body doesn't overproduce.

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.A: System, Balance, Assessment, Review
options.B: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Activity, Rate
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Safety, Behavior, Assessment, Response

explanation: SBAR is a standardized communication tool that helps healthcare workers share critical patient information clearly and concisely during handovers. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h6)

question: Why is taking corticosteroids together with NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) a big risk?

options.A: It causes blood pressure to drop dangerously low.
options.B: It cancels out the steroid so it doesn't work.
options.C: It greatly increases the chance of stomach ulcers and bleeding.
options.D: It stops the liver from filtering other drugs.

explanation: Brilliant! Both drugs irritate the stomach lining. Combining them multiplies the risk of painful ulcers and internal bleeding.

question: When programming an electronic IV infusion pump on the ward, what unit of measurement do you normally use?

options.A: Milliliters per hour (mL/hr)
options.B: Liters per 24 hours (L/day)
options.C: Drops per minute (gtt/min)
options.D: Drops per second (gtt/sec)

explanation: Spot on! Pumps are designed to deliver a precise volume of fluid every hour, so we program them in mL/hr.

question: What usually happens if a family planning client never returns for follow-up checks?

options.A: They will experience guaranteed protection from sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They will automatically switch to a permanent surgical method
options.C: They may stop using their method incorrectly or face unmanaged side effects
options.D: They are required by law to pay a large financial penalty

explanation: Without our guidance during follow-ups, clients often struggle with side effects or make mistakes using their contraception, which makes them give up on it.

question: What is the main goal of electrical cardioversion for a patient with a rapid, dangerous heart rhythm?

options.A: To permanently destroy the atrioventricular node
options.B: To reset the heart back to a normal sinus rhythm
options.C: To measure the exact cardiac output of the ventricles
options.D: To widen narrowed coronary arteries instantly

explanation: Cardioversion is like hitting 'restart' on a glitchy computer. It delivers a timed electrical shock to stop the chaos and let the heart's natural pacemaker take back control.

question: As a student nurse, which action best supports a patient receiving end-of-life palliative care?

options.A: Focusing strictly on lab results rather than emotional needs
options.B: Listening openly to their fears and helping them find personal meaning
options.C: Telling them not to worry about dying and changing the subject
options.D: Restricting family visits to keep the patient completely isolated

explanation: Being a compassionate listener and validating a patient's feelings offers immense comfort during their final days.

question: Why is keeping an eye on intracranial pressure (ICP) so vital after a severe head injury?

options.A: To prevent the patient from experiencing chronic back pain
options.B: To determine when the patient is ready for solid foods
options.C: To calculate the exact number of calories the brain burns daily
options.D: To make sure enough blood flows to the brain despite swelling

explanation: When the brain swells inside the skull, high pressure can pinch blood vessels closed and cut off vital oxygen. Monitoring helps us prevent brain starvation.

question: What is the best reason to place a healthy newborn skin-to-skin on mum's chest right after birth?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need to dry the baby with warm towels
options.B: It allows the nurse to perform the complete physical head-to-toe exam faster
options.C: It prevents the infant from passing meconium before the placenta is delivered
options.D: It helps maintain the newborn's body temperature and encourages early breastfeeding

explanation: Mum's chest is like a natural incubator! Skin-to-skin keeps baby warm and wakes up those natural instincts to latch and breastfeed.

question: How many milligrams are in a single gram?

options.A: 100 milligrams
options.B: 1,000 milligrams
options.C: 10 milligrams
options.D: 1,000,000 milligrams

explanation: Remember that 'milli' means one-thousandth. So, it takes 1,000 milligrams to make one full gram.

question: What is the primary underlying cause of coronary artery disease?

options.A: Inflammation of the outer sac surrounding the heart
options.B: Dilation and weakening of the heart muscle walls
options.C: Sudden infection of the inner heart lining
options.D: Buildup of fatty plaque inside the coronary arteries

explanation: Coronary artery disease develops primarily when cholesterol and other fats form plaque inside the arteries supplying the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h1)

question: In occupational health, what does a 'zoonotic disease' mean?

options.A: Mental stress from aggressive office management
options.B: Hearing damage caused by loud farm animals
options.C: An infection passed from animals to humans
options.D: A skin rash caused by laboratory chemicals

explanation: Zoonotic diseases are infections that naturally jump from animals to humans—something vets, farmers, and abattoir workers need to watch out for.

question: Your patient takes a traditional herbal remedy along with their prescribed blood pressure drugs. What should you do?

options.A: Explore the cultural significance of the remedy and check for potential drug interactions
options.B: Confiscate the herbal preparation during the home visit
options.C: Tell the patient immediately that traditional remedies are completely useless
options.D: Ignore the herbal remedy since it is not part of the hospital chart

explanation: Never dismiss cultural practices! Respect the patient while smartly checking to ensure the herbs won't clash with their prescribed medications.

question: What step immediately follows the physician writing a prescription in the unit dispensing workflow?

options.A: The pharmacist reviews and verifies the order
options.B: The ward cleaner organizes the medication cart
options.C: The nurse administers the drug immediately
options.D: The patient pays the hospital cashier

explanation: Before any medication is picked or packaged, the pharmacist must check the prescription for safety and correct dosing. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the most crucial detail to write in your nursing notes after a washout?

options.A: The favorite food of the patient's family
options.B: The volume and appearance of the fluid returned
options.C: The weather conditions outside the hospital
options.D: The exact brand name of the lubricant used

explanation: Always document what came out! Recording the amount and look of the return proves that the procedure worked and was safe.

question: Why did Florence Nightingale place the most severely injured soldiers closest to the nurse's station?

options.A: To make it easier for doctors to perform sudden surgeries
options.B: To keep them away from noisy convalescing soldiers
options.C: To comply with strict military hierarchy rules
options.D: To allow for closer and more frequent observation

explanation: Placing the sickest patients near the nurses allowed staff to detect rapid changes in condition early. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which sign might mean a patient's bowel was accidentally injured during laparoscopy?

options.A: Mild itching around the small skin puncture sites
options.B: Severe, worsening abdominal pain and rigidity
options.C: Low-grade shoulder pain when taking a deep breath
options.D: Temporary hoarseness of the patient's voice

explanation: Spot on! If the bowel leaks contents into the tummy, it causes an infection (peritonitis) marked by severe pain and a tight, hard (rigid) belly.

question: What is the main difference between BEmOC and CEmOC facilities?

options.A: BEmOC handles medical management and simple procedures without major surgery
options.B: CEmOC facilities never provide newborn resuscitation services
options.C: CEmOC centers only offer outpatient antenatal consultations
options.D: BEmOC facilities routinely perform elective surgical sterilizations

explanation: Think of BEmOC as handling medications, simple births, and first aid, while CEmOC takes on major surgeries and blood transfusions.

question: What is the expected effect of acute blood loss on a patient's pulse rate?

options.A: The pulse rate stays completely normal until death occurs
options.B: The pulse rate drops sharply to conserve remaining blood
options.C: The pulse rate increases to maintain blood pressure
options.D: The pulse rhythm becomes permanently irregular and slow

explanation: When blood volume drops, the body compensates by increasing the heart rate to keep vital organs supplied with blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which types of medications most commonly increase the risk of falls in older adults?

options.A: Multivitamins
options.B: Topical antifungal creams
options.C: Sedatives and antihypertensives
options.D: Vitamin C supplements

explanation: Drugs that cause dizziness, sleepiness, or sudden drops in blood pressure can easily lead to a fall. Always keep an eye on safety!

question: Why do we need multiple organizations teaming up to prevent unsafe abortions?

options.A: No single healthcare facility has the resources to handle all community reproductive needs alone
options.B: Government policies require every clinic to report pregnancy tests to the police
options.C: Hospitals are legally prohibited from providing contraceptive counseling directly to teenagers
options.D: Community groups refuse to work with doctors unless funded by international donors

explanation: Exactly! Tackling big public health issues means sharing resources, ideas, and reach across different groups so no one clinic has to carry the whole load.

question: What should a nurse do first when planning health education for a patient from a different cultural background?

options.A: Insist that the patient follow hospital routines strictly at home
options.B: Hand out standard English brochures without discussing them
options.C: Assume the patient already knows basic community health rules
options.D: Assess the patient's language, literacy level, and cultural beliefs

explanation: Education only works if the nurse understands how the patient communicates and what they believe about health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why can a long-lasting seizure harm brain cells?

options.A: The brain burns through oxygen and sugar faster than blood can supply them
options.B: Excessive GABA production causes neurons to drown in cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: Blood flow to the brain completely stops during the entire episode
options.D: The skull shrinks rapidly due to increased intracranial pressure

explanation: That's right! Continuous brain firing is hard work. It creates a massive energy demand, leading to oxygen shortage and exhaustion if not stopped.

question: When starting a routine IV line, where should you look first on the patient's arm?

options.A: The most proximal sites on the arm
options.B: The large veins near the neck
options.C: The most distal veins of the hand
options.D: The deep veins close to the core

explanation: Always start down on the hands (distal) and work your way up the arm later if needed. This saves the upper veins for future use!

question: A discharged mother struggles to afford nutritious food for her infant. Which action by the nurse best shows community-focused care?

options.A: Advising her to stop feeding the infant until she finds a better job
options.B: Referring the mother to a local community food program or welfare service
options.C: Keeping the infant admitted in the acute hospital ward indefinitely
options.D: Telling her to buy more expensive imported baby formula immediately

explanation: Connecting the family to local community assistance helps solve the root social cause of their nutritional challenge. You're being a true advocate!

question: What is a major lung complication that often happens to patients who are unconscious and immobile for a long time?

options.A: Hypostatic pneumonia
options.B: Pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Asthma exacerbation
options.D: Spontaneous pneumothorax

explanation: Keep learning! When patients stay still, fluids pool at the back of their lungs, making it easy for bacteria to grow and cause pneumonia.

question: What is the main goal when public health workers investigate a sudden disease outbreak?

options.A: To punish individuals who failed to maintain hygiene
options.B: To document medical billing records for the hospital
options.C: To manufacture new vaccines for the infected population
options.D: To find the exact source and stop the outbreak from spreading

explanation: Detective work is a huge part of nursing! Finding the source quickly lets health teams step in and protect the rest of the community.

question: Why must nurses monitor patients for several hours after a CT scan with contrast media?

options.A: The kidneys stop producing urine entirely for the rest of the day.
options.B: Delayed allergic reactions can sometimes occur after the procedure.
options.C: Delayed muscle spasms frequently happen due to table positioning.
options.D: The patient will lose all sensation in their limbs as the dye wears off.

explanation: While most allergic responses happen right away, some hypersensitivity reactions can be delayed, making post-procedure monitoring an important safety measure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why are metabolic and endocrine disorders considered such a big deal for public health?

options.A: They only affect elderly populations in rural areas
options.B: They are easily cured with a single antibiotic
options.C: They cause widespread and systemic complications
options.D: They never require long-term medical management

explanation: Because our hormones control so many different body systems, when something goes wrong here, it affects the whole body. Great thinking!

question: What term describes the official power attached to a management role that lets you give orders and make decisions?

options.A: Accountability
options.B: Authority
options.C: Specialisation
options.D: Responsibility

explanation: Authority is that official backing of your position that says, 'Yes, you have the green light to direct this process and make the call.'

question: How does the water seal chamber stop air from rushing back into the patient's chest?

options.A: It uses electronic suction to block all backward movement of gases
options.B: It freezes the tubing shut whenever the patient tries to breathe in
options.C: It creates a chemical barrier that destroys outside bacteria instantly
options.D: It acts as a one-way valve that lets air out but not back in

explanation: Think of it like a one-way street! Air bubbles out when the patient breathes out, but the water blocks outside air from getting back in.

question: During a quick nursing assessment, which of these is an early warning sign that a patient is struggling to breathe?

options.A: Use of accessory muscles to breathe
options.B: Warm and dry skin on the extremities
options.C: A slow and irregular heart rate
options.D: Normal resting respiratory rate

explanation: Spot on! When breathing gets tough, patients start using their neck and shoulder muscles to help pull air in.

question: A child is forced to weave in a dark room for twelve hours daily. What category of trafficking is this?

options.A: Commercial sex trade
options.B: Illegal adoption
options.C: Domestic servitude
options.D: Forced child labor

explanation: Working long hours in production or hazardous trades falls under forced child labor rather than house chores.

question: Why do facial stitches need to be removed much sooner than stitches on a knee or back?

options.A: Facial skin is much thicker than skin on the back
options.B: The face heals faster due to a rich blood supply
options.C: Stitches on the face cause less scarring if left longer
options.D: Facial muscles do not move during daily activities

explanation: The abundant blood supply in the head and neck allows rapid healing, requiring early suture removal to prevent track marks. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h6)

question: What should a nurse tell a patient to expect regarding bleeding after taking these medications?

options.A: Expect bleeding that is heavier than a normal menstrual period with some clots
options.B: Expect only light spotting that stops entirely within two hours
options.C: Expect continuous heavy hemorrhaging that requires immediate blood transfusion
options.D: Expect no bleeding until at least one week after taking misoprostol

explanation: Since the body is clearing out the uterine lining and tissue, heavier bleeding with a few clots is expected and part of the process.

question: Which nursing care helps stop joint stiffness in an unconscious patient?

options.A: Frequent administration of diuretics
options.B: Passive range-of-motion exercises
options.C: Keeping the patient flat on the back
options.D: Applying warm compresses to the chest

explanation: Spot on! Gently moving their arms and legs through their normal motion keeps the joints flexible while they can't move on their own.

question: What major expense directly increases shipping and freight costs when moving food to market?

options.A: Fuel prices
options.B: Fertilizer taxes
options.C: Crop insurance
options.D: Seed patents

explanation: Vehicles rely heavily on fuel, so higher fuel prices directly inflate the cost of transportation. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h5)

question: What does 'anticipatory grief' mean for caregivers of patients with degenerative illnesses?

options.A: Grief felt in advance as they watch their loved one slowly decline
options.B: Anger at the medical team for failing to find a genetic cure
options.C: Relief that the patient's physical illness will soon be over
options.D: Confusion about how to fill out insurance and hospital forms

explanation: Spot on. Caregivers often mourn the gradual loss of their loved one's personality and skills long before the person actually passes away. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h6)

question: When is the best time to start palliative care for someone with a serious illness?

options.A: After the patient is discharged to a nursing home
options.B: Exclusively during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.C: Early in the disease process alongside curative treatments
options.D: Only when all curative treatments have failed

explanation: Great thinking! Palliative care isn't just for the very end. It works best when started right alongside regular medical treatments from the time of diagnosis to support the patient all through their journey.

question: What happens in the chest when your diaphragm contracts during a breath in?

options.A: The pleural space fills entirely with air
options.B: Positive pressure forces air out of the lungs
options.C: Negative pressure is created to pull air in
options.D: Pressure inside the chest equals atmospheric pressure

explanation: When the diaphragm moves down, it opens up space and lowers the pressure inside, drawing air naturally into your lungs. Beautiful concept to master!

question: Why is a mini-laparotomy often performed immediately after a vaginal delivery?

options.A: The postpartum uterus is still enlarged, placing the tubes close to the abdominal wall.
options.B: Hormonal changes during birth make the patient immune to surgical site infections.
options.C: Regional anesthesia used for labor completely paralyzes the fallopian tubes.
options.D: Postpartum bleeding prevents the need for any internal stitching of tissues.

explanation: Shortly after birth, the anatomical position of the reproductive organs allows for a very small incision to easily access and tie the tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h4)

question: What is the main goal of doing a slit-lamp examination?

options.A: To wash out dust from the lower eyelid
options.B: To get a close-up, magnified view of the front of the eye
options.C: To measure exact distance vision
options.D: To check the patient's full side vision

explanation: The slit-lamp shines a bright, magnified light on front eye structures like the cornea, iris, and lens so you can see them clearly.

question: An 85-year-old retired civil servant comes to the clinic with joint pain and feeling very lonely. Which government program can help with both issues?

options.A: Giving them a heavy-duty vehicle driving license
options.B: Enrolling them in mandatory military training
options.C: Sending them to a full-time industrial workshop
options.D: Geriatric care integration and social protection programs

explanation: Great choice! Specialized geriatric care treats their physical aches, while social programs step in to beat loneliness and build community connection.

question: A shortage of which mineral leads to an enlarged thyroid gland, known as a goiter?

options.A: Iodine
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Iron
options.D: Zinc

explanation: You got it! Iodine helps the thyroid gland make important hormones. Without enough iodine, the thyroid swells up, causing a goiter. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h2)

question: What do we call the path germs use to leave their reservoir?

options.A: Mode of transmission
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Portal of exit

explanation: Just like leaving a room through a door, germs use a 'portal of exit' (like coughing or through body fluids) to leave their host.

question: During which phase of the nurse-patient relationship do you first meet the patient and build trust?

options.A: Evaluation phase
options.B: Working phase
options.C: Orientation phase
options.D: Termination phase

explanation: Think of the orientation phase as your first introduction! It's where you say hello, explain your role, and start building that initial trust.

question: What should the nurse do first before having a patient step onto a mechanical weighing scale?

options.A: Measure the height of the patient
options.B: Ask the patient to drink a glass of water
options.C: Clean the platform with strong bleach solution
options.D: Check that the scale is zeroed on a flat surface

explanation: Ensuring the scale rests on a hard, level surface and points to zero prevents false readings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h3)

question: How is a painful muscle abscess caused by an unsterile injection usually managed?

options.A: Apply tight bandages to squeeze the trapped fluid out through the skin
options.B: Massage the lump firmly to help disperse the pus into surrounding tissue
options.C: Assist with surgical incision and drainage while maintaining sterile dressings
options.D: Advise the patient to ignore the lump until it dissolves on its own

explanation: Trapped pus has to come out! An abscess requires sterile incision and drainage, followed by proper wound care and antibiotics to help the patient heal.

question: Why must nurses watch for child abuse in every family, rich or poor?

options.A: Child maltreatment occurs across all backgrounds regardless of status
options.B: Wealthy families are statistically more prone to emotional abuse
options.C: Lower-income families rarely report physical injuries
options.D: Government policies mandate screening only in high-poverty areas

explanation: Abuse doesn't care about money or social class. Keep an open mind and screen everyone, no matter their background!

question: A young, unmarried woman leaves a clinic without birth control because the nurse scolds her. What is this barrier called?

options.A: Healthcare provider bias
options.B: Supply chain failure
options.C: Geographic isolation
options.D: Commodity stock-out

explanation: When personal judgments or scolding from healthcare staff stop a client from getting care, that is provider bias. As future nurses, we always want to keep our clinics welcoming and judgment-free!

question: Why is a GTT often preferred over a simple fasting blood glucose test during pregnancy?

options.A: It is completed in under fifteen minutes with only a single blood draw
options.B: It catches hidden metabolic problems that show up only after a sugar challenge
options.C: It poses zero risk of causing nausea or dizziness in pregnant women
options.D: It requires no prior fasting or dietary restrictions from the expectant mother

explanation: Gestational diabetes often presents only when the body is stressed with a glucose load, making the dynamic test necessary. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h1)

question: What is the most crucial piece of history to gather first when assessing an animal bite?

options.A: The exact weight and age of the bitted patient
options.B: The color and breed of the animal involved
options.C: The insurance and home address of the owner
options.D: The exact time of the bite and tetanus status

explanation: Timing tells us about infection risks, while checking the patient's tetanus status lets us know if a booster shot is urgently needed.

question: Why is smooth care coordination so important when a patient leaves the hospital to go home?

options.A: It ensures the patient never needs to see a doctor again
options.B: It reduces the working hours of the nursing staff
options.C: It prevents fragmented services and medication errors
options.D: It completely eliminates the cost of medical supplies

explanation: Good coordination prevents dangerous gaps in treatment and stops confusing medication mix-ups during transition periods. Smooth teamwork saves lives!

question: What is the chief complaint in a patient health history?

options.A: The nurse's official medical diagnosis
options.B: The results of the patient's blood work
options.C: The main reason the patient is seeking care
options.D: A list of all medications taken in the past year

explanation: The chief complaint captures the primary problem or symptom that brought the patient to the hospital or clinic. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h3)

question: Taking a patient's height, weight, and body mass index (BMI) falls under which type of assessment?

options.A: Environmental data review
options.B: Clinical physical inspection
options.C: Anthropometric measurement
options.D: Biochemical laboratory test

explanation: Spot on! "Anthropometric" is just the clinical term for measuring the size, weight, and proportions of the human body.

question: Which dangerous electrolyte imbalance is most life-threatening in advanced kidney failure?

options.A: Hyponatremia
options.B: Hypocalcemia
options.C: Hypermagnesemia
options.D: Hyperkalemia

explanation: High potassium (hyperkalemia) is a major emergency because it messes with the heart's electrical rhythm and can lead to sudden cardiac arrest if not treated quickly.

question: How does electricity move through the heart in a biphasic defibrillator?

options.A: It circles around the heart chambers in a clockwise pattern
options.B: It travels forward through the heart and then reverses direction
options.C: It splits into multiple smaller pulses sent simultaneously
options.D: It flows in a single direction from the apex to the base

explanation: Biphasic means two phases! The current travels through the heart in one direction and then quickly switches and flows back through, making it super effective.

question: Why is it so important to involve a speech-language pathologist early after a brain injury?

options.A: To prescribe appropriate mobility braces and walking frames
options.B: To coordinate home healthcare insurance and discharge funding
options.C: To manage chronic joint pain and muscle spasms in the limbs
options.D: To check for safe swallowing before the patient eats or drinks

explanation: Safety first! SLPs make sure patients can swallow food and water without choking, while also helping them find ways to communicate their needs.

question: What is a major consequence when health workers judge teenagers seeking reproductive advice?

options.A: Adolescents immediately change their behavior and practice strict abstinence
options.B: Young people report the healthcare workers to international health bodies
options.C: Teenagers stop seeking professional help and turn to unsafe alternatives
options.D: Parents take over the health education role completely at home

explanation: Stigma and judgmental attitudes drive vulnerable youths away from clinics, leading to hidden risks like unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which test measures the exact number of HIV particles floating in the blood?

options.A: Viral load test
options.B: Basic metabolic panel
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: CD4 cell count

explanation: A viral load test counts how many copies of the virus are in the blood sample. Spot on!

question: Who is considered the primary client for a community health nurse?

options.A: The attending physician
options.B: The hospitalized patient
options.C: The local government authority
options.D: The entire community

explanation: Great job thinking big picture! Unlike bedside nursing that focuses on one patient at a time, community health nurses look at the health of the whole population in an area.

question: Why do intramuscular (IM) injections usually absorb faster than subcutaneous (SC) shots?

options.A: Muscles are located closer to the major organs of the body.
options.B: Skeletal muscle tissue has a richer blood supply than fat tissue.
options.C: Subcutaneous fat layers actively repel water-soluble medications.
options.D: Muscle tissue contains more digestive enzymes to break down tablets.

explanation: Muscles have lots of blood vessels (a rich blood supply) which quickly wash the medication away into circulation. Fat tissue has less blood flow.

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for making and producing breast milk?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Remember: Pro-lact-in promotes lact-ation (milk production)! It's the key hormone driven by the pituitary gland to make milk happen.

question: What is the best nursing trick for a moderate Alzheimer's patient who keeps forgetting to eat full meals?

options.A: Leave a large plate of hot food on the bedside table for hours
options.B: Rely entirely on intravenous fluids for daily nutrition
options.C: Provide frequent nutritious finger foods that are easy to handle
options.D: Insist that the patient sit at the table until the entire plate is empty

explanation: You nailed it! Finger foods make eating much easier for patients who struggle with utensils or lose focus during long meals. Practical nursing at its best!

question: A nurse notices that a surgical drain has produced 300 mL of bright red blood in the last hour. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Strip the tubing vigorously to clear out any remaining blood clots
options.B: Elevate the collection bag above the level of the patient's wound
options.C: Document the normal finding and check the patient again tomorrow
options.D: Notify the surgeon immediately because this suggests active hemorrhage

explanation: A sudden, large volume of bright red drainage indicates heavy bleeding inside the body, which requires urgent medical intervention. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h4)

question: Why do community health nurses conduct home visits for high-risk families?

options.A: To enforce strict fines on parents who fail to pay their taxes
options.B: To remove all children permanently from homes experiencing poverty
options.C: To monitor child development and assess safety hazards in the living environment
options.D: To conduct major surgical procedures without hospital equipment

explanation: Correct! Home visits help nurses see how children are living, check for safety issues, and offer supportive guidance to the family.

question: What attitude should you as a nurse always maintain when caring for patients with post-abortion complications?

options.A: Skeptical, inquisitive, and publicly critical
options.B: Empathetic, confidential, and free from moral judgment
options.C: Strict, punitive, and emotionally detached
options.D: Indifferent, passive, and task-oriented only

explanation: You're doing great. Being non-judgmental and keeping things strictly confidential builds trust, ensuring vulnerable patients feel safe enough to get lifesaving help.

question: Why should you and your patient set nutrition goals together instead of you just giving orders?

options.A: Patients are more likely to follow goals they helped create
options.B: Patients always know more about clinical nutrition than nurses
options.C: Hospital policies legally prohibit nurses from choosing diet plans
options.D: Collaborative goals eliminate the need for future follow-up visits

explanation: Exactly! When patients have a say in their plan, they feel a sense of ownership and are way more likely to stick with it.

question: In stroke care, what does 'spasticity' mean?

options.A: Rapid wasting away of muscle tissue
options.B: Complete loss of all muscle sensation
options.C: Uncontrolled trembling during resting states
options.D: Involuntary muscle stiffness and tight spasms

explanation: Spot on! Spasticity is when muscles become tight and stiff because of nerve damage, making them hard to stretch out.

question: What is a common social penalty for a family that refuses FGM in a pro-FGM community?

options.A: Severe ostracism and social isolation
options.B: Mandatory community service penalties
options.C: Permanent banishment from public schooling
options.D: Immediate imprisonment by local chiefs

explanation: That's right. Families who break this tradition often face intense rejection and loneliness from people around them.

question: Why is testicular torsion treated as an urgent medical emergency?

options.A: It causes an immediate permanent drop in total body testosterone
options.B: It always spreads a severe bacterial infection to the bladder
options.C: It triggers rapid enlargement of the prostate gland
options.D: It cuts off blood supply and can damage the tissue

explanation: When the spermatic cord twists, it blocks blood flow to the testicle. This is an emergency because the tissue needs oxygen fast to prevent permanent damage!

question: Which serious complication involves kidney failure and red blood cell damage after certain bacterial infections?

options.A: Congestive heart failure
options.B: Acute respiratory distress
options.C: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Hemolytic uremic syndrome

explanation: Certain nasty bacterial toxins can attack tiny blood vessels, leading to a dangerous mix of kidney trouble, low platelets, and anemia.

question: Why is it dangerous to use the total volume of a multi-dose liquid bottle when calculating a single dose?

options.A: Total volume measurements are always written in incorrect metric units
options.B: Liquid medications lose their potency once the safety seal is broken
options.C: The total volume is the container size, not the active drug concentration per dose
options.D: Manufacturers change the concentration levels daily inside the same bottle

explanation: Exactly! If you use the whole bottle's volume instead of the concentration per unit, you could accidentally cause a massive overdose.

question: In financial management, what is a "variance"?

options.A: The variation in patient recovery times across different wards
options.B: The difference between budgeted amounts and actual financial outcomes
options.C: The total amount of profit made from pharmacy sales alone
options.D: The legal penalty given to hospitals for missing safety records

explanation: A variance is simply the gap between what you planned to spend in your budget and what you actually spent in reality.

question: Why do international health authorities want every country to have clear national policies on medical waste?

options.A: To ensure uniform taxation of hospital supplies
options.B: To establish legal accountability and standardize safe handling practices
options.C: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment
options.D: To replace local hospital management boards with global inspectors

explanation: National rules give hospitals the legal backing and clear steps they need to handle dangerous materials safely every single day.

question: What is the main purpose of a living will?

options.A: To outline specific medical treatments a person wants or rejects
options.B: To appoint a lawyer to handle hospital bills
options.C: To give doctors permission to override family wishes
options.D: To distribute a person's property and money after death

explanation: Think of a living will as a person's voice on paper before they get too sick to speak. It clearly states the treatments they want or do not want in a medical emergency.

question: Which position is most commonly used when giving an adult patient an enema?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: Supine position
options.C: High Fowler's position
options.D: Sims position

explanation: Sims is a side-lying position with the top leg bent. It gives you a safe, clear view and easy access to the rectum.

question: What is a tough ethical situation a home-birth midwife might face during an emergency?

options.A: A client refusing a recommended transfer to a hospital facility
options.B: Deciding which brand of delivery gloves to purchase
options.C: Having too many medical doctors volunteering at a home birth
options.D: Complaining about the weather conditions during labor

explanation: It's a tricky balance! You must respect a patient's choices, but your clinical duty is to keep mom and baby safe when danger arises.

question: How can clinical nurses positively influence waste management practices on their wards?

options.A: By writing national environmental laws in parliament
options.B: By driving the municipal garbage trucks on weekends
options.C: By buying new incineration machines for the hospital
options.D: By acting as role models and teaching junior staff correct sorting

explanation: Spot on! Your daily good habits teach junior colleagues and students how to do things the right way.

question: What is the best everyday advice a nurse can give to help prevent chronic constipation?

options.A: Take a strong saline purgative every morning before breakfast
options.B: Reduce all fluid intake to allow stools to form more slowly
options.C: Avoid eating local foods like beans and green vegetables
options.D: Increase intake of water, dietary fiber, and physical activity

explanation: Simple and natural is best! Drinking water, eating fiber, and staying active keep the digestive tract happy and regular.

question: How do nurses use prevalence data when seeking funding from health ministries?

options.A: To demonstrate the total burden of disease and justify resource requests
options.B: To calculate the exact birth date of every infected community member
options.C: To replace physical examinations during routine home visits
options.D: To prove that no further medical supplies are required in the region

explanation: Showing the total number of people affected helps justify why funding and materials are urgently required. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h6)

question: Why is clear and prompt documentation of vital signs especially important in a busy Nigerian ward?

options.A: It guarantees that the patient will be discharged early
options.B: It ensures safe continuity of care when shifts change
options.C: It replaces the need to give a verbal handover report
options.D: It prevents patients from asking questions about treatment

explanation: Accurate written records give incoming nursing staff reliable information to safely monitor patients without missing critical changes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which Nigerian law sets the main minimum standards for factory safety and worker welfare?

options.A: The National Health Insurance Act
options.B: The Land Use Act
options.C: The Criminal Code Act
options.D: The Factories Act

explanation: You'll see this often in Nigerian public health! The Factories Act is the key law that protects workers and regulates safety conditions in Nigerian workplaces.

question: What is the medical term for pain felt during sexual intercourse?

options.A: Dysmenorrhea
options.B: Dyspareunia
options.C: Dysuria
options.D: Dystocia

explanation: Break it down: 'Dys-' means painful, and 'pareunia' relates to intercourse. It's a key symptom to ask about gently during health histories.

question: Why is family planning counseling so important before a mother is discharged from the postpartum ward?

options.A: Ovulation can occur before the first postpartum menstrual period returns
options.B: Sexual intercourse is strictly forbidden for a full year
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives are required to stop lochia flow
options.D: Pregnancy is impossible during the first six months postpartum

explanation: Many women are surprised to learn that an egg can be released (ovulation) before their monthly period ever comes back. Early advice helps them plan safely!

question: Why was the Basel Convention created back in the late 1980s?

options.A: Global hospitals were running out of space for medical syringes
options.B: Oceans were overflowing with plastic beverage containers
options.C: Air pollution from factories caused a sudden rise in global temperatures
options.D: Industrialized nations were dumping toxic waste in developing countries

explanation: Spot on! Wealthy countries used to ship their toxic industrial byproducts to poorer nations to save money. Public outrage over this unfair practice led directly to the treaty.

question: You notice a patient's GCS score dropped from 14 to 10 over two hours. What should you do right away?

options.A: Document the score in the chart and leave the room for a break.
options.B: Administer a strong sleeping pill to calm the restless patient.
options.C: Wait another four hours to see if the patient wakes up naturally.
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider immediately and report the neurological decline.

explanation: A dropping GCS score is an urgent red flag! Any sudden decline in a patient's alertness means you must alert the doctor right away.

question: Why is keeping a strict fluid balance chart so vital for a Lassa fever patient?

options.A: To prevent both dehydration and dangerous fluid overload leading to pulmonary edema
options.B: To calculate the exact amount of oral medication required daily
options.C: To ensure the patient loses weight while admitted in the isolation ward
options.D: To test the concentration of protein present in the blood plasma

explanation: Because leaky blood vessels make fluid management tricky, too little fluid causes shock, while too much fills the lungs.

question: What term describes the condition where semen flows backward into the urinary bladder during climax?

options.A: Erectile failure
options.B: Azoospermia
options.C: Hypospadias
options.D: Retrograde ejaculation

explanation: Retrograde ejaculation happens when the bladder neck fails to close properly, forcing semen backward instead of forward. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h4)

question: Why are newer drugs like solifenacin given just once a day?

options.A: They eliminate all risks of dry mouth and blurry vision
options.B: They dissolve instantly in the stomach lining
options.C: They completely bypass the liver metabolism process
options.D: They have a longer half-life to maintain steady control

explanation: Drugs with a longer half-life stay in the system longer, giving steady relief all day and making it easier for patients to remember their meds.

question: A patient arrives struggling to breathe and has blue lips after inhaling toxic fumes. What is your very first nursing priority?

options.A: Ask family members what chemical was spilled
options.B: Draw blood samples for a complete blood count
options.C: Ensure a patent airway and provide high-flow oxygen
options.D: Document the exact time of the workplace accident

explanation: Always remember ABC! Saving a life by securing the airway and giving oxygen comes way before asking questions or running tests.

question: Which test checks the speed and strength of electrical signals in a peripheral nerve?

options.A: Lumbar puncture
options.B: Nerve Conduction Studies
options.C: Electromyography
options.D: Magnetic Resonance Imaging

explanation: Nerve Conduction Studies use gentle, tiny electrical pulses on the skin to see how fast signals travel down the nerve highway.

question: What kind of organism causes amoebiasis?

options.A: A multicellular roundworm
options.B: A rapid-spreading virus
options.C: A single-celled parasite
options.D: A drug-resistant bacteria

explanation: Spot on! Amoebiasis is caused by a tiny, single-celled protozoan parasite. You've got this!
